name: eng-2296
title: Simplify the Roam import dialog and import feedback

prepare.why: the Obsidian test vault published three claims to the eng-2329-demo group

nodes.title: Daylight exposure resets the circadian clock
nodes.body: Morning light shifts melatonin onset earlier.

nodes.title: Caffeine after noon delays sleep onset
nodes.body: Half-life is five to six hours.

prepare.why: none of the three claims, nor their type, was imported into this graph before

check.js: !["discourse-graph/nodes/PK Import Claim", "PKC - Daylight exposure resets the circadian clock", "PKC - Caffeine after noon delays sleep onset", "PKC - Cool bedrooms improve deep sleep"].some((title) => proof.page.exists(title))

apply.js: proof.page.remove(["discourse-graph/nodes/PK Import Claim", "PKC - Daylight exposure resets the circadian clock", "PKC - Caffeine after noon delays sleep onset", "PKC - Cool bedrooms improve deep sleep"])

prepare.why: the extension has a local database session for this graph, since the local create-space edge function is down

cases.title: The import result links every imported node
cases.caption: Import two shared claims. The result now lists each imported node as a link, not only the ones with warnings.

steps.why: open import the way a user would

do.wait_for: .bp3-dialog tbody tr:has-text("Daylight exposure resets the circadian clock")

steps.why: wait for the shared node's row

do.click: .bp3-dialog tbody tr:has-text("Daylight exposure resets the circadian clock") label.bp3-checkbox
.bp3-dialog tbody tr:has-text("Caffeine after noon delays sleep onset") label.bp3-checkbox

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const callout = proof.byText('.bp3-dialog .bp3-callout', 'imported'); if (!callout) return false; const links = Array.from(callout.querySelectorAll('li a')).map((link) => link.innerText); return callout.innerText.includes('2 imported') && links.some((text) => text.includes('Daylight exposure')) && links.some((text) => text.includes('Caffeine after noon')); }, { what: 'a result listing both imported claims as links', timeout: 20000 })

cases.title: Imported nodes leave the table
cases.caption: Imported nodes leave the table, as in Obsidian's import, so only the claim still to import is left.

steps.why: look at the table under the result

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog tbody tr')).map((row) => row.innerText); return rows.some((text) => text.includes('Cool bedrooms')) && !rows.some((text) => text.includes('Daylight exposure') || text.includes('Caffeine after noon')); }, { what: 'only the unimported claim in the table' })

cases.title: Clicking a result opens the page and closes the dialog
cases.caption: Clicking a result opens that page and closes the dialog.

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => !proof.dialogs().length && Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.rm-title-display')).some((title) => proof.visible(title) && title.innerText.includes('Daylight exposure resets the circadian clock')), { what: 'the imported page open with the dialog closed' })

cases.title: Reopening import still hides what's already imported
cases.caption: Open import again: the two imported claims stay hidden. A newer version comes in through Refresh instead.

expect.js: (() => { const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.bp3-dialog tbody tr')).map((row) => row.innerText); proof.assert(!rows.some((text) => text.includes('Daylight exposure') || text.includes('Caffeine after noon')), 'An imported claim is still in the table.'); })()
